note: THE NUGGET CLEAN-PLATE CANDIDATE (opening-set retrofit phase 1, doc 36 Q116). An edit of the shipping plate with the people gone and the finish changed toward Room 5, so the composition is the shipping room's by construction: the street wall with the batwing doors and window on the left, the bar running away down the right, the back wall closing it about two-thirds up. EVERY RECT HERE WAS RE-READ FROM SCRATCH on art/staging/room-03/clean-plate-02/candidate-1920x864.png on a 100 px grid (the shipping annotation's hotspotsNote says the candidate is re-read from scratch, and it was). A CANDIDATE: the shipping room is untouched; this compiles to nugget_candidate, reachable only by the dev warp, for Tyler's review.
walkableNote: The floor's back edge is the foot of the far wall as the candidate draws it (the chairs' feet at y 500, the piano's foot at 520, the doorway threshold at 600-690 by the batwings). The right edge follows THE BAR FRONT AND ITS THREE STOOLS, which are painted into the plate and sit in front of the counter (stool feet at 1180/680, 1330/740, 1570/830): floor Thad cannot walk through, oak or stool. Until a stool is cut as its own occluder (§13 separation plan) he walks round them, never behind them, so the room occludes nobody -- the same answer the shipping room gives, now for a reason that is written down. The near corner stops at x 1400 so the spittoon (1400-1490) lies wholly outside the floor: the first compile carved a 14 px sliver beyond it that nothing could reach.

scaling.note: TYLER'S TWO ANCHORS, KEPT. The candidate is the shipping composition by construction (an edit, not a new picture), so the depth curve Tyler set against that composition -- 198 at the back wall so his head is nowhere near the chandelier, 459 at the frame's foot -- carries over unchanged; the far anchor moves 8 px down with the re-read floor edge and nothing else. WHAT THE PLATE'S OWN PERSPECTIVE SAYS, for the review: the painted furniture implies a taller man -- the bar stools read 420 at y 680, 455 at y 740 and 490 at y 830, the upright piano's 265 px reads ~350 at its foot, the doorway's 590 px reads ~470 at the door -- so a 1.75 m man at the far wall would be ~330 by the furniture, and at 198 he stands a head shorter than the piano. The same tension existed in the shipping room (the seated card players' heads implied ~270) and Tyler chose 198 for the chandelier. A DECISION POINT for the plate review, not a change made here.

lampsNote: NO CHANDELIER LAMP. Doc 16: the chandelier is not lit, and the candidate paints its candles cold. A lamp declaration would breathe a pool under a thing the writing says is dark, which is exactly the contradiction the shipping room carried (it declared a chandelier pool of 0.1 over the middle of the room). The practical-light hierarchy is the stove first, the bar lamps second, the door lamp third, and the blue street through the doors, which is not a lamp.

occlusion.note: PLANNED, NOT CUT (Tyler's order: masks only after the plate is selected). The candidate offers real occluders the shipping plate never had: the three bar stools (1180-1270 x 500-680, 1330-1430 x 545-740, 1570-1700 x 620-830), the spittoon (1400-1490 x 765-864) and the near end of the counter. None is in use: the floor's right edge stops at the stools, so Thad never passes behind them, and every band is masked by nothing. When a stool is cut as a plane the floor may extend along the bar and the bands re-declare their planes.
